feature: Edit a loaded company without changing the active books
policy: Behavior-only fictional observations; original Bookr implementation and wording. No vendor source, executable inspection, file format or artwork is used.

browserCommands.execution: One full chain after the unit suite

verificationResult.promotedSource: 17 focused model/lifecycle units followed by 11 grouped editor browser checks passed on the actual source
verificationResult.screenshots: Seven editor captures bind visible content to saved fictional API data; desktop and 320/390 layouts reviewed
verificationResult.previewAudit: Three API-bound screenshots on the existing preview; GET only, zero attempted writes and page errors, saved data and session unchanged
verificationResult.money: 100000 paise sale minus 40000 paise receipt retains 60000 paise outstanding; all accounting rows unchanged
verificationResult.limits: Behavior and content checks do not establish native pixel equality. The State picker remains unpublished.

study.evidenceRetention: Original runtime observations and verification artifacts are retained privately outside the published repository.
verified: The edit selector lists loaded companies only.
Choosing an inactive loaded company opens that company's own profile and calendar without making it active.
Cancel returns to the edit selector with the target highlighted and its name in the search input.
Saving only mailing metadata returns to the same selector for both inactive and active targets; reopening shows the saved metadata.
The previously active company and its working date and reporting period remain unchanged.
limits: Runtime save studies changed mailing metadata only. They do not establish rules for changing accounting dates, currency, tax or security.
State-picker empty-query Escape remains unverified and is excluded from this feature.

included: Concurrency and financial isolation regression coverage

selector.reuse: Existing company selector DOM, IDs, layout and keyboard controller; add edit as an explicit mode.
selector.initialFocus: Search input; active company ID is the preferred highlighted target when present.
selector.returnFocus: Search input prefilled with the edited target's latest name; highlight by target ID rather than list position or name.
selector.search: Trimmed case-insensitive name substring; update matching rows without mutating source catalog or loaded IDs.
selector.allCompanies: Existing all-company selection action remains select mode; it must not turn an edit into an unloaded-company edit or activate a target automatically.
selector.empty: Show an empty result and reject Enter without issuing a target request.

keys.Enter: Open highlighted target for edit when mode is edit
keys.Escape: Return to the existing Company menu

profile.open: GET /api/companies/:targetId immediately before rendering the form; do not use a stale catalog profile.
profile.identity: Form, heading, immutable calendar, PUT URL and revision bind to the selected target ID, independently of the active API header.
profile.defaults: Preserve fresh target values. Do not replace existing values with active-company defaults.
profile.validation: Retain existing Bookr metadata validation, nonempty name, maximum lengths, known profile keys and server revision checks; no additional accounting rules are inferred.

keys.Escape: Existing nonempty-field clearing and reusable discard confirmation; confirmed cancel returns to the edit selector
keys.Escape on discard dialog: Choose No and preserve the draft

save.request: PUT /api/companies/:targetId with the freshly fetched target revision; X-Bookr-Company remains the previously active company.
save.success: Mark the returned profile published; refresh catalog and active-book display through read-only requests, then return to edit selector with saved target name/query/ID selected.
save.session: Never call lifecycle.select, location.reload or company activation for edit-save/cancel. Preserve loaded IDs, active ID, working date and current period.
save.displayRefresh: Refresh catalog and existing active-book presentation only; this updates active-company names if the active target was renamed without replacing the session.
save.prepublicationFailure: Keep draft and target identity; re-enable fields. A 409 keeps the stale draft available and reports conflict without silently reloading, overwriting or reissuing PUT.
save.postpublicationFailure: If any subsequent GET fails after PUT succeeded, retain the published target and disabled fields, report that save succeeded, and offer read-only refresh retry. Retry performs GET only; never repeat PUT, activate a company or treat the published form as unsaved.
save.canonicalPublication: Immediately after PUT succeeds, synchronize the disabled form fields, target heading and form target-ID/revision attributes from the returned canonical profile before issuing follow-up GETs. The server trims metadata; published fields must show those saved values even when a later catalog/state GET fails. Keep that saved profile across GET-only retries.
save.recoveryGeometry: The recovery command label and Ctrl+A shortcut must be completely visible and clickable within its existing footer button at desktop, 320px and 390px widths. Use a short original label without changing the shared footer layout.
save.existingFlows: Create and restore keep their existing published Open Company retry behavior; do not merge that activation recovery into edit recovery.
save.pending: Use existing request lifetime and navigation guards; prevent duplicate acceptance during save/refresh.

pureModel.contract: Pure projection of catalog, loaded IDs, explicit mode, query and preferred target ID into sorted visible rows and highlighted target/index; no DOM, API, storage or mutation.
pureModel.selectionStability: Preserve preferred target ID across renamed or resorted fresh catalog rows when visible; otherwise use the first visible row, with no selected ID for empty results.
pureModel.returnQuery: Obtain the current target name by ID from refreshed catalog, rather than retaining a stale name.

accountingEffect.effect: None. This feature changes company metadata only, using the existing validated endpoint.
invariants: No vouchers, ledger balances or outstanding amounts change
No cross-company book reads or writes through a mistaken target
All monetary amounts remain integer paise
The original fictional sale 100000 paise less receipt 40000 paise remains 60000 paise outstanding
